title: Cohen structure theorem: a complete local ring has a coefficient ring
statement: Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring which is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring] (the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ is bijective), and let $p\ge0$ be the characteristic of the residue field $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$. Then $R$ has a *coefficient ring*: a subring $\Lambda\subseteq R$ such that (1) $\Lambda$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m$ and is $(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)$-adically complete; (2) the map $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\to R/\mathfrak m$ induced by the inclusion is an isomorphism; (3) $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m=p\Lambda$ (so $\Lambda$ is a field when $p=0$).

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), part (1), and its proof (paragraphs 1-2: lifting $\kappa$ resp. a Cohen ring $\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ through $R/\mathfrak m^n$ by formal smoothness, Proposition 0322 characterize-separable-field-extensions, Lemmas 0328 cohen-rings-exist, 0329 cohen-ring-formally-smooth); coefficient ring: Definition Tag 0326 (definition-coefficient-ring, line 44837); complete local ring: Definition Tag 0324 (definition-complete-local-ring, line 44786)

proof.text: (Notation; the square-zero kernels; the base rings.) Write $\kappa=R/\mathfrak m$, $\pi_n:R/\mathfrak m^n\to R/\mathfrak m^{n-1}$ ($n\ge2$) for the projections and $r_n:R/\mathfrak m^n\to\kappa$ for the reductions. For $n\ge2$ the kernel of the surjection $\pi_n$ is $J_n=\mathfrak m^{n-1}/\mathfrak m^n$, and $J_n^2=0$ since $\mathfrak m^{2(n-1)}\subseteq\mathfrak m^n$ ($2n-2\ge n$); $\pi_n$ identifies $(R/\mathfrak m^n)/J_n$ with $R/\mathfrak m^{n-1}$. If $p=0$: for every integer $N\ge1$ the image of $N\cdot1$ in $\kappa$ is nonzero, so $N\cdot1\notin\mathfrak m$ and $N\cdot1$ is a unit of the local ring $R$; hence there is a unique ring map $\mathbf Q\to R$, all the rings $R/\mathfrak m^n$, $\kappa$ are $\mathbf Q$-algebras through it, and every ring homomorphism between $\mathbf Q$-algebras is $\mathbf Q$-linear (it is determined on $\mathbf Q$ by $1\mapsto1$). If $p>0$: $p\cdot1$ maps to $0$ in $\kappa$, so $p\in\mathfrak m$ and $p^n\in\mathfrak m^n$; hence $p^n=0$ in $R/\mathfrak m^n$, so $R/\mathfrak m^n$ (and its quotient $R/\mathfrak m^{n-1}$) is a $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$-algebra, and ring homomorphisms between such rings are $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z$-linear.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraphs 1-2 (the kernels of $R/\mathfrak m^n\to R/\mathfrak m^{n-1}$ and the maps $\mathbf Q\to R/\mathfrak m^n$, $\mathbf Z/p^n\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ in the two diagrams, left implicit there)

proof.text: (Case $p=0$: compatible sections $\varphi_n$.) We construct ring homomorphisms $\varphi_n:\kappa\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ ($n\ge1$) with $r_n\circ\varphi_n=\mathrm{id}_\kappa$ and $\pi_n\circ\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}$ ($n\ge2$). Put $\varphi_1=\mathrm{id}_\kappa$. Given $\varphi_{n-1}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-formally-smooth] to the extension $\kappa\supseteq\mathbf Q$ (a field of characteristic $0$), with $D=R/\mathfrak m^n$, the square-zero ideal $J=J_n$ and $g=\varphi_{n-1}:\kappa\to D/J_n=R/\mathfrak m^{n-1}$, a $\mathbf Q$-algebra homomorphism by step 1: there is a ring homomorphism $\varphi_n:\kappa\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ with $\pi_n\circ\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}$; then $r_n\circ\varphi_n=r_{n-1}\circ\pi_n\circ\varphi_n=r_{n-1}\circ\varphi_{n-1}=\mathrm{id}_\kappa$. (Formal smoothness is the lifting property of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for the ideal $\mathfrak n=0$.)

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 1 (induction on $n$, the first diagram, using Proposition 0322)

proof.text: (Case $p=0$: the limit and the coefficient field.) The family $(\varphi_n)_n$ is compatible with the projections, so $a\mapsto(\varphi_n(a))_n$ is a ring homomorphism $\kappa\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; composing with the inverse of the canonical map $R\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$, a ring isomorphism since $R$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], gives a ring homomorphism $\varphi:\kappa\to R$ with $\varphi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m^n=\varphi_n(a)$, in particular $\varphi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m=a$. Let $\Lambda=\varphi(\kappa)$. As $\kappa$ is a field and $\varphi(1)=1\ne0$, $\varphi$ is injective and $\Lambda\cong\kappa$ is a field. If $\varphi(a)\in\mathfrak m$ then $a=\varphi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m=0$; so $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m=0=p\Lambda$, which is (3). $\Lambda$ is a local ring with maximal ideal $0=\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m$, and it is $0$-adically complete (the canonical map $\Lambda\to\varprojlim_n\Lambda/0$ is bijective, the system being constant), which is (1). The map $\Lambda=\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\to R/\mathfrak m$ sends $\varphi(a)$ to $a$, so it is the inverse of the isomorphism $\varphi:\kappa\to\Lambda$, which is (2).

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 1, last sentence ('Putting these maps together ... gives a map whose image is the desired coefficient ring'; the verification of (1)-(3) of Definition 0326 is written out here)

proof.text: (Case $p>0$: a Cohen ring and compatible maps $\varphi_n$.) By [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-rings-exist] choose a Cohen ring $\Lambda_0$ (a discrete valuation ring with maximal ideal $p\Lambda_0$, $p\Lambda_0$-adically complete) and an isomorphism $\varepsilon:\Lambda_0/p\Lambda_0\xrightarrow{\sim}\kappa$. Let $\rho_n:\Lambda_0/p^n\Lambda_0\to\Lambda_0/p^{n-1}\Lambda_0$ and $\sigma_n:\Lambda_0/p^n\Lambda_0\to\Lambda_0/p\Lambda_0$ be the reductions. We construct ring homomorphisms $\varphi_n:\Lambda_0/p^n\Lambda_0\to R/\mathfrak m^n$ with $\pi_n\circ\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}\circ\rho_n$ ($n\ge2$) and $r_n\circ\varphi_n=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_n$. Put $\varphi_1=\varepsilon$. Given $\varphi_{n-1}$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth] (formal smoothness of $\mathbf Z/p^n\mathbf Z\to\Lambda_0/p^n\Lambda_0$) with $D=R/\mathfrak m^n$ (a ring with $p^nD=0$ by step 1), the square-zero ideal $J=J_n$ and the ring homomorphism $g=\varphi_{n-1}\circ\rho_n:\Lambda_0/p^n\Lambda_0\to R/\mathfrak m^{n-1}=D/J_n$: there is a ring homomorphism $\varphi_n$ with $\pi_n\circ\varphi_n=\varphi_{n-1}\circ\rho_n$. Then $r_n\circ\varphi_n=r_{n-1}\circ\varphi_{n-1}\circ\rho_n=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_{n-1}\circ\rho_n=\varepsilon\circ\sigma_n$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 2 (choice of a Cohen ring by Lemma 0328, induction on $n$ with the second diagram, using Lemma 0329)

proof.text: (Case $p>0$: the limit map $\psi$.) For $a\in\Lambda_0$ the elements $\varphi_n(a\bmod p^n)\in R/\mathfrak m^n$ are compatible under the $\pi_n$ (step 4), so $a\mapsto(\varphi_n(a\bmod p^n))_n$ is a ring homomorphism $\Lambda_0\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]; composing with the inverse of the canonical isomorphism $R\to\varprojlim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$ ($R$ is $\mathfrak m$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]) gives a ring homomorphism $\psi:\Lambda_0\to R$ with $\psi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m^n=\varphi_n(a\bmod p^n)$. For $n=1$: $\psi(a)\bmod\mathfrak m=\varepsilon(a\bmod p)$. Since $\varepsilon$ is an isomorphism, $\psi(a)\in\mathfrak m$ if and only if $a\in p\Lambda_0$ (*). Put $\Lambda=\psi(\Lambda_0)$, a subring of $R$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 2, last sentence ('Putting these maps together $\lim_n\varphi_n:\Lambda=\lim_n\Lambda/p^n\Lambda\to R=\lim_nR/\mathfrak m^n$')

proof.text: (Case $p>0$: the kernel of $\psi$.) By (*) $\ker\psi\subseteq p\Lambda_0$. The ring $\Lambda_0$ is a Noetherian local domain whose maximal ideal is generated by the nonzero element $p$ ($\Lambda_0$ is a principal ideal domain, not a field), so by [lem-weil-pbc-dvr-unit-times-uniformizer-power] every nonzero $b\in\Lambda_0$ is $b=up^m$ with $u$ a unit and $m\ge0$, and $b\Lambda_0=p^m\Lambda_0$. Hence if $\ker\psi\ne0$, with $N$ the least exponent $m$ occurring for its nonzero elements, $p^N\in\ker\psi$ and $\ker\psi=p^N\Lambda_0$, with $N\ge1$ as $\ker\psi\subseteq p\Lambda_0$. So either $\psi:\Lambda_0\to\Lambda$ is an isomorphism, or $\ker\psi=p^N\Lambda_0$ for some $N\ge1$ and $p^N\Lambda=\psi(p^N\Lambda_0)=0$.

source.place: Algebra, Theorem Tag 032A (theorem-cohen-structure-theorem, line 44929), proof, paragraph 2, last sentence; the three cases of the remarks after Definition 0326 (Algebra, lines 44850-44867: $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring, or Artinian with maximal ideal generated by $p$), written out here

proof.text: (Case $p>0$: $\Lambda$ is a coefficient ring.) (3): by (*), $\psi(a)\in\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m$ iff $a\in p\Lambda_0$, so $\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m=\psi(p\Lambda_0)=p\Lambda$. (1), locality: $p\Lambda\subseteq\mathfrak m$ is a proper ideal ($1\notin\mathfrak m$), and an element $\psi(a)\in\Lambda\setminus p\Lambda$ has $a\notin p\Lambda_0$, so $a$ is a unit of the local ring $\Lambda_0$ (maximal ideal $p\Lambda_0$) and $\psi(a)$ is a unit of $\Lambda$; hence $\Lambda$ is local with maximal ideal $p\Lambda=\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m$. (2): the composite $\Lambda_0\xrightarrow{\psi}\Lambda\to\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\to R/\mathfrak m$ is $a\mapsto\varepsilon(a\bmod p)$ (step 5), surjective; so $\Lambda/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)\to R/\mathfrak m$ is surjective, and it is injective because its kernel is $(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)/(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)=0$. (1), completeness: $(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)^n=p^n\Lambda$. In the first case of step 6, $\psi:\Lambda_0\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda$ carries $p^n\Lambda_0$ onto $p^n\Lambda$ for all $n$, and $\Lambda_0$ is $p\Lambda_0$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring], so the canonical map $\Lambda\to\varprojlim_n\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is bijective. In the second case $p^n\Lambda=0$ for $n\ge N$, so the system $(\Lambda/p^n\Lambda)_n$ is constant equal to $\Lambda$ from $n=N$ on and the canonical map $\Lambda\to\varprojlim_n\Lambda/p^n\Lambda$ is bijective (an element of the limit is determined by its component at $n\ge N$). So $\Lambda$ is $(\Lambda\cap\mathfrak m)$-adically complete, and $\Lambda$ is a coefficient ring of $R$.

lean.statement: theorem exists_coefficient_subring (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsLocalRing R] [IsAdicComplete (maximalIdeal R) R] (p : ℕ) [CharP (ResidueField R) p] : ∃ (Λ : Subring R) (hΛ : IsLocalRing Λ), letI : IsLocalRing Λ := hΛ maximalIdeal Λ = (maximalIdeal R).comap Λ.subtype ∧ IsAdicComplete ((maximalIdeal R).comap Λ.subtype) Λ ∧ Function.Bijective (Ideal.quotientMap (I := (maximalIdeal R).comap Λ.subtype) (maximalIdeal R) Λ.subtype le_rfl) ∧ (maximalIdeal R).comap Λ.subtype = Ideal.span {(p : Λ)}
